skills.name: site-scorecard
skills.description: Grade a website A to F on speed, accessibility, broken links, structured data, and AI readiness, then deliver a one-page plain-English PDF scorecard with the top 3 fixes per check. Use when someone asks to check, audit, grade, or re-check a site.
skills.content:
---
name: site-scorecard
description: >-
  Grade a website A to F on speed, accessibility, broken links, structured data,
  and AI readiness, then deliver a one-page plain-English PDF scorecard with the
  top 3 fixes per check. Use when someone asks to check, audit, grade, or
  re-check a site.
---
## Inputs
- URL (required). Follow redirects and use the final URL.
- Mode: single page or whole site. Whole site is capped at 50 pages: same-origin URLs from /sitemap.xml, or crawl homepage links if there's no sitemap. Speed samples the first 5 pages in site mode.
- Optional competitor URL: run the same scorecard and add a side-by-side grade row.

## Toolkit (free, no keys), build on the box if missing
In a workdir: `npm i playwright @axe-core/playwright && npx playwright install chromium`. A runner script takes `<url> <single|site> <outDir>` and writes results.json; a report script grades it and writes scorecard.html plus the PDF. Wrap each check so one failure never stops the others.

1. Speed (rate limits matter here)
   - The keyless PageSpeed Insights API (`https://www.googleapis.com/pagespeedonline/v5/runPagespeed?url=<u>&strategy=mobile&category=performance`) shares a tiny anonymous quota and usually returns HTTP 429. Expect that.
   - If env `PSI_API_KEY` is set (a free Google Cloud key), append `&key=$PSI_API_KEY` and use PSI as primary. Space calls 2 s apart, one at a time.
   - Without a key: try PSI at most twice (wait 15 s, then 30 s), then stop retrying.
   - Fallback: local Lighthouse 12 mobile, `npx -y lighthouse@12 <u> --only-categories=performance --output=json --quiet --chrome-flags="--headless=new --no-sandbox"` (CHROME_PATH = Playwright's chromium). Run 3 times per page, use the MEDIAN score and metrics (single local runs swing ~10 points). Pages sequentially, never in parallel.
   - Label the source on the scorecard: "Google PageSpeed" or "Lighthouse, measured locally (median of 3)". Tell the owner local runs can read a bit harsher than Google's and offer a re-check with a free key.
   - Keep perf score, LCP, CLS, TBT, FCP, LCP element, top opportunities.
2. Accessibility: per page, new browser context, `new AxeBuilder({page}).withTags(['wcag2a','wcag2aa','wcag21a','wcag21aa']).analyze()`. Aggregate violations by rule with impact and node count.
3. Links: from the rendered DOM collect a[href], img[src], stylesheets, scripts; dedupe, cap 500. Be polite: max 10 concurrent, max 3 per host, HEAD then GET, 15 s timeout. On 429 honor Retry-After (cap 30 s) and retry once; still 429/403 = "bot-blocked, not broken", listed separately. >=400 or no response = broken. (linkinator misses JS-built sites and hangs on Node 20.)
4. Structured data: parse every application/ld+json block (record invalid), flatten @graph, collect @type; record title, meta description, og: tag count.
5. AI readiness: fetch /llms.txt (200, non-HTML, non-empty = present; empty = 'empty') and /robots.txt. Flag AI crawlers (GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, Applebot-Extended) blocked by Disallow: /. Note a Sitemap: line.

Whole-site and competitor runs: load pages one at a time, ~1 s apart, so the host or CDN doesn't throttle you.

## Grading rubric
- Speed (mobile perf): A 90+, B 75-89, C 50-74, D 35-49, F <35.
- Accessibility penalty (per rule: critical 10, serious 5, moderate 2, minor 1): A 0, B <=5, C <=15, D <=30, F >30. Any critical caps at D.
- Broken links % (bot-blocked excluded): A 0, B <=1, C <=3, D <=5, F >5.
- Structured data (5 pts): valid JSON-LD on every page 2; Organization/WebSite/LocalBusiness-type schema 1; title+meta description everywhere 1; >=3 OG tags 1. 5=A 4=B 3=C 2=D <=1=F.
- AI readiness (5 pts): non-empty llms.txt 2; robots.txt 1; sitemap in robots 1; no AI crawlers blocked 1. Same mapping.
- Overall: average (A4..F0): >=3.5 A, >=2.5 B, >=1.5 C, >=0.5 D, else F. Exclude ungraded checks and say so.

## Layout
HTML to a one-page Letter PDF via Playwright page.pdf({printBackground:true}). Header with URL, mode, date, big overall grade. One card per check: colored letter, one plain sentence with the key number, at most 3 'Top fixes' written for a marketer (no jargon). Speed card names its data source. Footer: how grades work plus the caveat. Verify Pages: 1 with pdfinfo; if it spills, shorten text, never drop a check. Render a PNG and look before sending.

## Accessibility caveat (always include)
Automated tools catch only part of accessibility issues (roughly a third to a half). A good grade isn't proof of compliance; recommend a keyboard and screen-reader pass.

## When a check fails
Mark it 'Not graded', explain why in one plain sentence, exclude it from the overall, offer to re-run. Never invent or estimate a grade. If the site won't load at all, stop and tell the owner.

## Deliver
Send the PDF with a short summary: overall grade, weakest check, the single most valuable fix. Keep results.json so monthly re-checks can show changes.

skills.name: site-scorecard-getting-started
skills.description: First conversation with a new owner: collect their site, scope, optional competitor, and re-check preference one question at a time, then run the first scorecard.
skills.content:
---
name: site-scorecard-getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation with a new owner: collect their site, scope, optional
  competitor, and re-check preference one question at a time, then run the first
  scorecard.
---
Introduce yourself in one line: you check their website and give a plain-English A to F scorecard for speed, accessibility, broken links, structured data, and AI readiness, with the top fixes for each.

Ask one question at a time, waiting for each answer:
1. "What's your website address?" (Check it loads; if not, ask them to confirm it.)
2. "Should I check just that one page, or the whole site? Whole site covers up to 50 pages and takes longer."
3. "Is there a competitor you'd like to compare against? Totally optional. Paste their URL or say skip."
4. "Want me to re-check every month and tell you what changed?"

Then:
- Save a memory with their site URL, mode, competitor (if any), and re-check preference.
- If yes to monthly, create a routine on the 1st of each month: "Run @site-scorecard on <URL> in <mode> mode (plus competitor if set), compare grades to last month, and send the PDF with what improved or slipped."
- Run @site-scorecard now and send the first PDF with a short summary: overall grade, weakest area, and the one fix to do first.
